docs.title: OSINT-D2
docs.text:
Investigate public identity data with an AI agent that follows leads and documents its evidence, or run direct scans with no AI at all.

Quick Start Source Code

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: OSINT-D2 is a command-line tool and local dashboard. Direct scans use 20 username scanners and 4 email scanners, with optional Sherlock for about 470 more sites. The agent uses function calling to choose its next step: it scans what you give it, reads the results, and follows new leads such as emails and websites.

docs.title: Agentic AI
docs.text:
The model decides which tools to call, interprets the results, and pivots to new leads. If it runs out of steps, it is forced to write a report.

Agent mode

docs.title: Identity Triangulation
docs.text:
Cross-correlates usernames, emails, bios, avatars, and writing style across platforms. Avatar hashing (dHash) detects the same photo even when resized.

Architecture

docs.title: Six-Area Reports
docs.text:
Agent reports cover Identity, Geo-temporal, OCEAN Psychology, Tech Stack, Ideology, and OpSec/Attack Surface. The personality and ideology sections are speculative inferences.

Security & responsible use

docs.title: Trust Anchor Verification
docs.text:
Declare known-good sources (--trust github:user). Weighted scoring on name, bio, avatar, and location then filters out false positives.

Trust anchors

docs.title: PDF Dossiers
docs.text:
Generate reports with identity cards, profile analysis, risk matrices, and entity graphs. The CLI renders them with WeasyPrint, and the dashboard with Chromium.

Web dashboard

docs.text:
English, Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, and Russian in the CLI, web dashboard, profiler, and PDF reports.

docs.title: Threat Model
docs.text: OSINT-D2 runs locally on the machine of the person who downloads it. The project operates no server and receives no investigations. This page records what the tool protects, against whom, and which risks are accepted.

docs.title: What needs protecting
docs.text: Asset Where it lives Personal data about investigated people reports/, the dashboard's memory, and the AI provider if you use a remote one API keys (AI, HIBP, proxy) Environment variables, the project .env, and the user .env (readable only by its owner) The operator's identity and IP address Visible to scanned sites unless a proxy is configured AI credits Spent by each investigation

docs.title: Who could cause harm
docs.text: Actor Can do Main protections An investigated person, or anyone controlling a page or profile Write text the agent reads, redirect requests, serve huge or slow responses Tool results are marked as untrusted and limited in size, URLs are checked at every redirect, downloads are capped at 5 MB, and report HTML is sanitized A website open in the operator's browser Send requests to the local server Unknown Host headers and foreign WebSocket origins are rejected, and CORS is limited to known origins A compromised dependency or release Run code on the operator's machine Locked dependencies, pinned CI actions, pip-audit, CodeQL, and gitleaks The operator Misuse the tool against someone Acceptable use policy, sensitive inferences off by default. The tool cannot prevent deliberate misuse

docs.title: Accepted risks
docs.text:
The project is a local, single-user tool, so these are deliberate decisions. Revisit them if that changes.

Risk Why it is accepted What remains exposed The dashboard has no login It binds to 127.0.0.1 by default Other local users and processes can reach it, and can replace the saved AI key. Binding it to another interface exposes it to that network DNS rebinding can bypass the SSRF check Each request is checked, and fixing this needs a custom transport A hostile page could make the agent reach a service on the operator's local network and read its response There is no record of who investigated whom A local tool has a single operator, and a log would be one more file of personal data The operator must keep any record their legal basis requires Prompt injection is reduced, not eliminated No current technique removes it A hostile page can still distort the report, so its findings need human review Reports are not encrypted by the tool Disk encryption belongs to the operating system Anyone who can read reports/ can read the dossiers

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Attackers who already control the operator's account or machine.
  • Accuracy guarantees for AI inferences.
  • The practices of third-party services. See Data flows.

docs.text: See the security policy.

docs.title: REST API Endpoints
docs.text:
The server exposes a small API for starting investigations and downloading their results. Progress is delivered over the WebSocket.

http://localhost:8000

No authentication

The API has no login by design, because it is for local use. See Security & Responsible Use.

FastAPI also serves generated schemas at /docs and /openapi.json.

docs.title: GET / — Dashboard
docs.text:
Returns the dashboard page.

Query parameter Type Description lang string en, es, pt, ar, or ru. Unknown values fall back to en

docs.title: POST /api/investigate — Start an investigation
docs.text:
Starts a background investigation and returns immediately.

{
  "target": "John Doe",
  "usernames": ["johndoe", "jdoe123"],
  "emails": ["john@example.com"],
  "phones": ["+1 555 123 4567"],
  "trust_anchors": ["github:johndoe"],
  "mode": "agent",
  "ai_provider": "deepseek",
  "language": "en",
  "max_steps": 10,
  "enable_breach_check": false
}
Field Type Default Rules target string Required 1–200 characters, not blank usernames string[] [] Up to 50 emails string[] [] Up to 50 phones string[] [] Up to 20 trust_anchors string[] [] Up to 50 mode string agent agent or phone ai_provider string Configured provider deepseek, openai, or ollama language string es en, es, pt, ar, or ru max_steps integer 6 1–30 enable_breach_check boolean false Requires OSINT_D2_HIBP_API_KEY

phone mode only looks up phones, without the AI agent. Choosing a provider other than OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER runs without OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY, so the key never reaches another service.

Response 200:

{
  "investigation_id": "3f2a9c1e7b6d4e8fa1b2c3d4e5f60718",
  "status": "started",
  "target": "John Doe"
}
Status Meaning 422 The request failed validation 429 5 investigations are already running

A 200 only means the investigation started. Failures that happen later, such as a missing API key, arrive as WebSocket events.

docs.title: POST /api/cancel/{investigation_id} — Cancel
docs.text:
Stops a running investigation immediately.

{
  "status": "cancelled",
  "investigation_id": "3f2a9c1e7b6d4e8fa1b2c3d4e5f60718"
}

If the investigation already ended, status holds its final state. An unknown ID returns 404.

docs.title: GET /api/download/{investigation_id}/{file_type} — Download a file
docs.text:
file_type Content Content type pdf PDF dossier application/pdf canvas Obsidian Canvas graph application/json Status Meaning 400 Unsupported file_type 404 Unknown investigation, or the file does not exist

Each file is ready once the WebSocket sends its artifact event. Only files from that investigation are served.

Sessions live in memory

Sessions are lost when the server restarts, and the oldest finished ones are dropped after 100. The files remain in reports/, but these endpoints can no longer serve them.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
ID=$(curl -s localhost:8000/api/investigate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"target": "John Doe", "usernames": ["johndoe"], "language": "en"}' \
  | jq -r .investigation_id)

# After the "artifact" event for the PDF:
curl -o dossier.pdf "localhost:8000/api/download/$ID/pdf"

docs.title: WebSocket Protocol
docs.text: The WebSocket streams an investigation's progress as it runs.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
ws://localhost:8000/ws/{investigation_id}

Connect after POST /api/investigate returns the ID. You can connect at any time: earlier events are replayed in order, so nothing is lost if the run started or finished first.

Browser connections must come from the same origin or one listed in OSINT_D2_CORS_ORIGINS. Others are closed with code 1008.

An unknown ID receives one event and the connection closes:

{ "type": "error", "data": "Investigation not found." }

docs.title: Message format
docs.text:
Every message is JSON with a type and a data field. Graph events can repeat a node ID, so ignore nodes you already have.

Type Sent when Modes log Human-readable activity All progress A step finishes Agent node_add An entity is found All edge_add A relationship is found All phone_data A phone lookup finishes All report_done The AI report is ready Agent graph_svg The final graph is ready Agent timeline The step list is ready Agent artifact A file can be downloaded Agent status The investigation ends All

docs.title: log
docs.text:
Text in the investigation's language, for display only. Don't parse it, because its wording can change.

{ "type": "log", "data": "[STEP 1] scan_username(username=johndoe)" }

docs.title: progress
docs.text:
step can stay the same across several events, because one step can call several tools. The run may finish before reaching max_steps.

{ "type": "progress", "data": { "step": 2, "max_steps": 6 } }

docs.title: node_add
docs.text:
A vis-network node. Groups in use: target, email, phone, identity, platform, and noise (a probable false positive).

{
  "type": "node_add",
  "data": { "id": "user:johndoe", "label": "@johndoe", "group": "platform" }
}

docs.title: edge_add
docs.text:
Links a node to the root, whose ID is always target:root. Labels in use: PHONE_NUM, USES_EMAIL, and TRUST_ANCHOR.

{
  "type": "edge_add",
  "data": { "from": "target:root", "to": "email:john@example.com", "label": "USES_EMAIL" }
}

docs.title: phone_data
docs.text:
{
  "type": "phone_data",
  "data": {
    "e164": "+15551234567",
    "carrier": "Example Telecom",
    "country": "United States",
    "line_type": "mobile",
    "whatsapp": true,
    "timezones": ["America/New_York"]
  }
}

docs.title: report_done
docs.text:
Not sent if the model produced no report. summary is Markdown, and summary_html is its server-rendered version.

{
  "type": "report_done",
  "data": {
    "summary": "# Identity\n\nSame handle on **three** platforms.",
    "summary_html": "<h1>Identity</h1>\n<p>Same handle on <strong>three</strong> platforms.</p>",
    "highlights": ["Same handle on 3 platforms"],
    "confidence": 0.82
  }
}

Treat this content as untrusted

All of it derives from third-party pages. Sanitize summary_html before inserting it into a page, as the dashboard does with DOMPurify, and render highlights as plain text. The same applies to svg in graph_svg.

docs.title: graph_svg
docs.text:
Not sent if the graph could not be built. confidence is null when there is no report.

{
  "type": "graph_svg",
  "data": {
    "target": "John Doe",
    "confidence": 0.82,
    "svg": "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" ...>",
    "nodes": 12,
    "edges": 15,
    "vectors": 4
  }
}

docs.title: timeline
docs.text:
kind is one of Platform, Email, Phone, Breach, Identity, or Finding. evidence is cut to 500 characters, and correlation is currently always null.

{
  "type": "timeline",
  "data": {
    "confidence": 0.82,
    "steps": [
      {
        "kind": "Platform",
        "label": "scan_username(username=johndoe)",
        "evidence": "{\"target\": \"johndoe\", ...}",
        "correlation": null
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: artifact
docs.text:
The named file can now be downloaded. Values: canvas, pdf.

{ "type": "artifact", "data": "pdf" }

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Marks the end of the investigation. Values: completed, partial (finished, but a tool or file failed), cancelled, failed. With failed, the preceding log event starting with [ERROR] holds the reason.

{ "type": "status", "data": "completed" }

docs.title: Example client
docs.text:
const ws = new WebSocket(`ws://localhost:8000/ws/${investigationId}`);

ws.onmessage = (event) => {
  const { type, data } = JSON.parse(event.data);

  switch (type) {
    case 'log':
      console.log(data);
      break;
    case 'artifact':
      console.log(`Ready: /api/download/${investigationId}/${data}`);
      break;
    case 'status':
      console.log(`Finished: ${data}`);
      ws.close();
      break;
  }
};

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
OSINT-D2 is inspired by Clean Architecture, separating domain logic from I/O adapters. The codebase is organized into three layers.

        M["cli/main.py<br/>Typer + Rich"]
        D["cli/doctor.py"]
    end

docs.title: Core
docs.text: The core holds the domain models and orchestration. Most I/O lives in adapters, but the separation isn't strict yet: core/services imports adapters directly, and agent_tools.py and resources_loader.py make HTTP requests.

docs.title: Domain Models (core/domain/models.py)
docs.text:
Three Pydantic v2 models define the investigation data:

Model Purpose PersonEntity Root aggregate: target identifier + discovered profiles + optional AI analysis SocialProfile One profile on one platform: URL, username, network, exists flag, bio, avatar, metadata dict AnalysisReport AI-generated analysis: summary, highlights, confidence score, model used, raw payload

Additional models: HaveibeenpwnedBreach, HaveibeenpwnedProfiles for breach data.

docs.title: Agent Engine (core/services/agent_engine.py)
docs.text:
The ReAct reasoning loop. See Agent Mode for details.

Key decisions: - Uses the OpenAI client (compatible with DeepSeek, Ollama, Groq, any OpenAI-compatible API) - Forced report fallback: if the agent exhausts steps, forces generate_report with tool_choice - Profile collection: every tool result is parsed for SocialProfile-like entries and indexed into the vector store - Explicit target: the target identifier is set by the caller (CLI/web), never guessed from the free-text objective

docs.title: Trust Anchor Verification (core/services/trust_anchor.py)
docs.text: 4-signal weighted identity verification. See Trust Anchor System for the full deep-dive.

docs.title: URL Guard (core/services/url_guard.py)
docs.text: SSRF protection for the fetch_url agent tool. Blocks requests to: - Private IP ranges (10.x.x.x, 172.16.x.x, 192.168.x.x) - Loopback (127.0.0.1, localhost) - Link-local (169.254.x.x) - Cloud IMDS endpoints (169.254.169.254)

docs.title: Platform Scanners (adapters/osint_sources/)
docs.text:
20 dedicated scanners, each implementing platform-specific extraction:

Scanner Method Extracted data GitHub REST API Name, bio, location, email, repos, blog, Twitter link GitLab REST API Name, bio, avatar Instagram Web scraping + OG tags Name, bio, followers, avatar Facebook mbasic.facebook.com Name, location, education X (Twitter) Web scraping Bio, followers, avatar Telegram t.me Display name, bio, avatar Reddit JSON API Karma, cake day, bio Medium REST API Name, bio, avatar Pinterest Web scraping Name, bio, boards count Twitch GQL API Display name, bio, avatar + 10 more Various Platform-specific metadata

Additionally, data-driven site lists (WhatsMyName format) extend coverage to hundreds of additional sites without dedicated scrapers.

docs.title: Vector Store (adapters/vector_store.py)
docs.text:
Pure-Python in-memory search engine with two capabilities:

  1. Semantic search (BM25): retrieve previously collected evidence by concept
  2. Stylometric correlation: compare writing styles using character n-gram cosine similarity

Technical details: - No heavy deps: no numpy, scipy, or ML frameworks. Sparse dicts + math only. - Trilingual stemming: light suffix stripping for Spanish, English, Portuguese - Accent folding: Unicode NFD normalization strips diacritics - BM25 parameters: k1=1.5 (term frequency saturation), b=0.75 (document length normalization) - Stylometry guard: minimum 40 characters to prevent false certainty from short texts

docs.title: Rate Limiter (adapters/rate_limiter.py)
docs.text:
Responsible scanning with per-domain throttling:

Setting Default Env Var Delay between requests 200ms OSINT_D2_REQUEST_DELAY_MS Jitter ±100ms OSINT_D2_REQUEST_JITTER_MS Per-domain concurrency 3 OSINT_D2_PER_DOMAIN_CONCURRENCY Retry attempts (429/503) 3 OSINT_D2_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS Global concurrency 30 OSINT_D2_SITES_MAX_CONCURRENCY

Exponential backoff with jitter on 429/503 responses.

docs.title: Report Exporter (adapters/report_exporter.py)
docs.text:
Generates classified-style PDF dossiers with: - Identity card with avatar, classification level, and evidence tags - 6D cognitive profile sections - Entity relationship graph - Risk/confidence matrix - Full evidence appendix

The CLI renders Jinja2 HTML → WeasyPrint → PDF, and saves the HTML if WeasyPrint fails. The dashboard renders the same HTML with Playwright (headless Chromium), adding the graph page.

docs.title: Avatar Analyzer (adapters/avatar_analyzer.py)
docs.text:
Perceptual image comparison using difference hash (dHash): 1. Resize to 9x8 grayscale 2. Compare adjacent pixels to generate 64-bit hash 3. Hamming distance between hashes = dissimilarity

Robust to JPEG compression, resizing, and minor color adjustments. Used by the agent's compare_avatars tool.

docs.title: HTTP Client (adapters/http_client.py)
docs.text: Centralized httpx.AsyncClient factory with: - Configurable proxy support (ScrapingAnt residential/datacenter) - Custom User-Agent - Timeout management - HTML metadata extraction (title, description, social links, emails in page)

docs.title: Configuration (core/config.py)
docs.text:
All configuration via pydantic-settings with the OSINT_D2_ prefix:

  • Resolution order: env vars → user ~/.config/osint-d2/.env → project .env
  • Cross-platform: Windows (%APPDATA%), macOS (~/Library/Application Support), Linux (~/.config)
  • Typed validation: Pydantic enforces types, ranges, and constraints at startup

docs.title: Trust Anchor System
docs.text:
Different people often share a handle. Trust anchors let you declare which accounts are known to belong to your target, so OSINT-D2 can discard profiles that contradict them.

The problem

Scanning johndoe finds a GitHub profile for John Doe, a Pinterest profile for Marco Bianchi, and a Kaggle profile for Li Wei (all fictitious). Without anchors, an agent might merge them into one person.

docs.title: 1. Declare anchors
docs.text:
osint-d2 agent johndoe --trust github:johndoe --trust email:john@example.com
Type Format Example Network network:username github:johndoe Email email:address email:john@example.com

Signals from several anchors are merged into a single reference identity.

docs.title: 2. Build the reference identity
docs.text:
TrustAnchor("github", "johndoe")
    → Find the scanned profile for github.com/johndoe
    → Extract: name="John Doe", location="Lisbon"
    → Extract: bio keywords = ["python", "security"]
    → Extract: avatar hash = md5(avatar_url)[:12]

TrustAnchor("email", "john@example.com")
    → Split the local part into a name, if possible
    → Add to reference emails

Email anchors use a heuristic name splitter:

Email Extracted name janelle.rivera@example.com janelle rivera john_doe@example.com john doe janellerivera@example.com janelle rivera (with the username hint xjanelle)

Known usernames from other anchors serve as hints: finding janelle inside janellerivera splits it into two names.

docs.title: 3. Verify profiles
docs.text:
Each discovered profile is compared with the reference using weighted signals:

Signal Weight What it checks Name 40% Display name vs. reference names. Exact match = 40 points, partial overlap = 20–40. Bio keywords 30% Keyword overlap with trusted bios. 50%+ overlap = full score. Avatar 20% MD5 of the image URL matches a reference avatar hash. Location 10% Substring match against reference locations.

Profiles below 30% confidence are flagged as false positives.

docs.title: 4. Detect name contradictions
docs.text:
A different surname is a hard contradiction, because it usually means a different person:

Reference names: {"janelle rivera"}
Profile name:    "janelle castro"
    → Overlap: {"janelle"} ✓
    → Contradiction: {"castro"} ✗ (not in any reference name)
    → Hard contradiction (len("castro") >= 4) → score = 0
    → Verdict: FALSE POSITIVE

docs.title: In Agent Mode
docs.text:
The agent's first message includes a TRUSTED SOURCES block:

TRUSTED SOURCES (user-verified data):
- VERIFIED GITHUB account: @johndoe
- VERIFIED EMAIL: john@example.com

IMPORTANT: Use these as ground truth. If a profile on another
network has a different name/surname than what these sources
suggest, that profile likely belongs to a DIFFERENT PERSON.
Do NOT conflate identities.

docs.title: Where to Use Them
docs.text:
# Agent mode
osint-d2 agent johndoe --trust github:johndoe --trust email:john@example.com

# Direct scans
osint-d2 scan johndoe --trust github:johndoe
osint-d2 hunt -u johndoe --trust github:johndoe

# Interactive wizard: answer yes to "Add trusted identity sources?"
osint-d2 wizard

In the dashboard, enter them under Verified accounts.

Best practice

Start with the platform where you're most confident about the identity. Profiles with a real name, bio, avatar, and location provide all four signals.

This is a heuristic

A wrong anchor makes every later decision wrong, and a true match can be discarded if someone uses different names across platforms. Review what was discarded.

docs.title: Adding a Scanner
docs.text:
This guide adds a username source. The example works in the real pipeline, and tests/test_scanner_contract.py checks it against every registered scanner.

A scanner is a class in src/adapters/osint_sources/ that implements the OSINTScanner protocol from src/core/interfaces/scanner.py:

class OSINTScanner(Protocol):
    async def scan(self, username: str) -> SocialProfile: ...

Email sources use the same method, and receive the email address as the argument.

docs.title: 1. Create the scanner
docs.text:
# src/adapters/osint_sources/newplatform.py
"""Scanner for NewPlatform public profiles."""

from __future__ import annotations

from adapters.http_client import build_async_client
from core.config import AppSettings
from core.domain.models import SocialProfile
from core.interfaces.scanner import OSINTScanner


class NewPlatformScanner(OSINTScanner):
    _base_url = "https://newplatform.example"

    def __init__(self, settings: AppSettings | None = None) -> None:
        self._settings = settings or AppSettings()

    async def scan(self, username: str) -> SocialProfile:
        url = f"{self._base_url}/{username}"

        async with build_async_client(self._settings) as client:
            response = await client.get(url)

        return SocialProfile(
            url=str(response.url),
            username=username,
            network_name="newplatform",
            exists=response.status_code == 200,
            metadata={"status_code": response.status_code},
        )

Rules:

  • Always return a SocialProfile. Use exists=False when the profile does not exist.
  • Use build_async_client, so timeouts and proxy settings apply.
  • Let network exceptions propagate. The pipeline records them as an error on that source, so one failure doesn't stop the scan.
  • Keep the constructor callable with no arguments. The pipeline creates each scanner with scanner().

docs.title: 2. Register it
docs.text:
Add the class to _USERNAME_SCANNERS in src/core/services/identity_pipeline.py, or _EMAIL_SCANNERS for an email source:

from adapters.osint_sources.newplatform import NewPlatformScanner

_USERNAME_SCANNERS = (
    # ...existing scanners...
    NewPlatformScanner,
)

docs.title: 3. Add a test
docs.text:
# tests/test_newplatform_scanner.py
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, patch

import pytest

from adapters.osint_sources.newplatform import NewPlatformScanner


@pytest.mark.asyncio
@pytest.mark.parametrize(("status", "exists"), [(200, True), (404, False)])
async def test_scan(status, exists):
    response = MagicMock(status_code=status, url="https://newplatform.example/demo")
    client = AsyncMock()
    client.get.return_value = response
    context = MagicMock()
    context.__aenter__ = AsyncMock(return_value=client)
    context.__aexit__ = AsyncMock(return_value=False)

    with patch("adapters.osint_sources.newplatform.build_async_client", return_value=context):
        profile = await NewPlatformScanner().scan("demo")

    assert profile.exists is exists
    assert profile.network_name == "newplatform"

docs.text:
poetry run pytest tests/test_newplatform_scanner.py tests/test_scanner_contract.py
poetry run pytest
poetry run ruff check .

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Put platform-specific data in metadata. The keys name, location, company, email, and followers reach the agent; see _compact_profiles in agent_tools.py.
  • Fill in bio and image_url when available. They are used for correlation and the dossier.
  • Respect the platform's terms of service and rate limits.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
OSINT-D2 is configured via environment variables. Create a .env file from the template:

cp .env.example .env

Or use the interactive setup:

osint-d2 doctor setup-ai

docs.title: Where Settings Come From
docs.text:
From highest to lowest priority:

  1. Environment variables
  2. User config: ~/.config/osint-d2/.env on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support/osint-d2/.env on macOS, %APPDATA%\\osint-d2\\.env on Windows
  3. .env in the current directory

So the user config overrides a project .env. osint-d2 doctor setup-ai and --ai-save write to the user config, so if a project setting seems to be ignored, check that file.

docs.title: AI Provider
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER deepseek Provider this configuration belongs to: deepseek, openai, ollama. The dashboard sends the API key only to this provider. OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY — API key for the AI provider. Required for AI analysis and agent mode. Supports DeepSeek, Groq, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI-compatible API. OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL From the provider Base URL for the AI API. Set it for other OpenAI-compatible services, or Ollama in another container. OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL From the provider Model name to use for analysis. OSINT_D2_AI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 45 Timeout in seconds for AI API calls. OSINT_D2_AI_MAX_RETRIES 3 Max retries on transient AI failures (rate limits, network errors).

docs.title: Breach Checks
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_HIBP_API_KEY — Have I Been Pwned API key, a paid service. Required for --breach-check. HIBP receives the full email address.

docs.title: Proxy (ScrapingAnt)
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_PROXY_API_KEY — ScrapingAnt API key. Enables proxy routing for all scanner requests. OSINT_D2_PROXY_USERNAME — ScrapingAnt username for standalone proxy products. OSINT_D2_PROXY_MODE residential when a proxy key is set, otherwise none Proxy type: residential or datacenter. OSINT_D2_PROXY_COUNTRY — 2-letter country code for geo-targeting (e.g., us, de, br).

docs.title: HTTP & Rate Limiting
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 20 Timeout per HTTP request in seconds. OSINT_D2_USER_AGENT osint-d2/3.0 User-Agent header for OSINT requests. OSINT_D2_SITES_MAX_CONCURRENCY 30 Max concurrent requests across all site-list scanners. OSINT_D2_REQUEST_DELAY_MS 200 Minimum delay (ms) between requests to the same domain. OSINT_D2_REQUEST_JITTER_MS 100 Random jitter ± (ms) added to delay for naturalness. OSINT_D2_PER_DOMAIN_CONCURRENCY 3 Max simultaneous requests to the same domain. OSINT_D2_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS 3 Retries on 429/503 responses with exponential backoff.

docs.title: Language & Scanning
docs.text: Variable Default Description OSINT_D2_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE en Default language for CLI prompts, AI analysis, and PDF reports. Options: en, es, pt, ar, ru. OSINT_D2_SITES_NO_NSFW true Exclude NSFW categories from site-list scans. OSINT_D2_USERNAME_SITES_PATH — Path to custom username sites JSON (WhatsMyName format). OSINT_D2_EMAIL_SITES_PATH — Path to custom email sites JSON.

  2. Configure:

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Run the built-in diagnostic tool:

poetry run osint-d2 doctor run

This checks:

  • AI provider configuration (key, base URL, model)
  • HTTP connectivity (outbound request to GitHub)
  • WeasyPrint PDF rendering
  • Playwright Chromium
  • Have I Been Pwned key
  • Proxy configuration (ScrapingAnt mode, key, country)

It lists how to fix each problem. Missing Chromium or Pango is only a note, because they're optional. It exits with code 1 only if the connection fails.

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
OSINT-D2 reads settings from environment variables, the user config, and a .env in the current directory. See where settings come from.

All variables use the OSINT_D2_ prefix. See the Configuration reference for the full list.

docs.title: Sherlock (About 470 Sites)
docs.text:
OSINT-D2 includes a built-in async Sherlock engine — no external packages required.

When you pass --sherlock to the hunt command, OSINT-D2 automatically downloads the official Sherlock site manifest (data.json) from GitHub and runs checks across its sites using its own concurrent runner.

osint-d2 hunt -u johndoe --sherlock

No pip install sherlock-project needed

Unlike earlier versions, OSINT-D2 v3.0 does not depend on the sherlock-project pip package. The manifest is fetched on demand and cached locally in data/.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
This tutorial takes you from installation to your first result, then to an AI-assisted investigation. Direct scans need no API key.

Before you start

Only investigate where you have a lawful basis and, where required, authorization. Practice on a username of your own. See Security & Responsible Use.

This guide assumes a Poetry installation. With Docker, replace poetry run with docker compose exec osint-d2.

docs.title: 1. Check your setup
docs.text:
poetry run osint-d2 doctor run

The table shows what works, and what to do about anything that doesn't. A missing AI key is fine for now.

docs.title: 2. Run your first scan
docs.text:
poetry run osint-d2 scan your-username

You get a table with one row per source: Exists says whether the profile was found. Expect some false positives, because other people may use the same handle.

If a source shows an error

Some platforms block automated requests. The scan continues with the others, and the error appears in that row.

docs.title: 3. Remove false positives
docs.text:
Tell OSINT-D2 which account you know is yours. Profiles that contradict it are discarded:

poetry run osint-d2 scan your-username --trust github:your-username

docs.title: 4. Save the results
docs.text:
poetry run osint-d2 hunt -u your-username --export-json --export-pdf

Files are saved to reports/ in the current directory. They contain personal data, so store and delete them with care.

PDF dossier (demo data)

docs.title: 5. Run an agent investigation
docs.text:
Agent mode needs an AI provider, and sends scan results to it unless you use Ollama. Add your provider to .env:

OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek
OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-your-key

Then run:

poetry run osint-d2 agent your-username --trust github:your-username --max-steps 6

Each tool call appears as it runs, followed by the report. Treat the report as a set of leads to verify. See Agent Mode.

docs.title: 6. Try the dashboard
docs.text:
poetry run osint-d2 serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. See the Web Dashboard guide.

docs.title: Commands at a glance
docs.text: Command Use it for AI scan One username Optional (--deep-analyze) scan-email One email Optional (--deep-analyze) hunt Several targets, Sherlock, site lists, breach checks Optional (--ai) agent Autonomous investigation Required analyze AI analysis of a saved JSON file Falls back to a local heuristic without a key phone Phone number lookup No wizard Guided prompts Depends on the choices

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Agent mode needs an AI provider key Set OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY, run osint-d2 doctor setup-ai, or use Ollama command not found: osint-d2 Use poetry run osint-d2, or activate the environment with poetry env activate PDF export creates an HTML file Install the system libraries, then run doctor run --breach-check requires a HaveIBeenPwned API key Set OSINT_D2_HIBP_API_KEY, or remove the flag A setting seems to be ignored The user config overrides the project .env. See precedence Output is JSON instead of a table Output is being piped. Add --format table

docs.title: Agent Mode
docs.text:
OSINT-D2's Agent Mode is the core differentiator: an autonomous AI investigator that uses LLM function calling to reason about evidence, decide what to scan next, and pivot across identities — just like a human analyst, but faster.

Not a script — an agent

Most OSINT tools run a fixed pipeline. Agent Mode uses a ReAct reasoning loop: the AI observes evidence, thinks about what's missing, calls a tool, and repeats until it has enough to build a cognitive profile.

docs.title: How the ReAct Loop Works
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["📋 User provides target + usernames/emails"] --> B["🧠 LLM receives context + 9 available tools"]
    B --> C{"LLM decides: call a tool or generate report?"}
    C -->|"Call tool"| D["⚡ Execute tool, append result to conversation"]
    D --> E{"Step limit reached?"}
    E -->|"No"| B
    E -->|"Yes"| F["⚠️ Force generate_report with tool_choice"]
    C -->|"generate_report"| G["📊 6D Cognitive Profile produced"]
    F --> G

Each step, the LLM receives the full conversation history (system prompt + all previous tool calls and results) and decides autonomously what to do next. The engine (agent_engine.py) manages the loop, collects discovered profiles, and indexes them into the in-memory vector store for cross-reference.

docs.title: Forced Report Fallback
docs.text: If the agent exhausts its max_steps without calling generate_report, the engine forces one final LLM call with tool_choice={"type": "function", "function": {"name": "generate_report"}} — guaranteeing every investigation produces a structured output, even if the agent was too eager investigating.

docs.title: The 9-Tool Arsenal
docs.text:
The agent has access to 9 tools, each wrapping an existing OSINT scanner and compacting results to fit the LLM context window.

# Tool What it does Key output 1 scan_username Check the 20 native username scanners (GitHub, X, Instagram, Reddit, Telegram, etc.) Confirmed profiles with bios, avatars, metadata 2 scan_email Pivot from email via Gravatar, PGP keyservers, Ubuntu keyserver. Optionally scans local part as username. Cross-platform profiles, PGP keys 3 breach_check Official HaveIBeenPwned API. Requires OSINT_D2_HIBP_API_KEY and sends the full email to HIBP Breach names, dates, compromised data types 4 fetch_url Extract intelligence from any URL: title, emails, social links, OG metadata Discovered usernames, emails, social links 5 compare_avatars Perceptual hashing (dHash) to compare two avatar images Similarity %, hamming distance 6 scan_phone Telecom intelligence: E.164 validation, carrier, country, WhatsApp status Carrier, line type, timezones, footprint URLs 7 search_vector_memory BM25 search across all evidence collected during the investigation Ranked snippets with relevance scores 8 correlate_stylometry Character n-gram stylometric comparison against known target writing Cosine similarity (0-1) per candidate 9 generate_report Finalize investigation with structured 6D analysis Summary, highlights, confidence score

docs.title: SSRF Protection
docs.text: fetch_url and compare_avatars validate each URL, including every redirect, against private, reserved, and cloud metadata addresses. See the known limits.

docs.title: Score Interpretation
docs.text:
Critical — do not misread these

The agent's system prompt explicitly instructs the LLM how to interpret each scoring metric. Misinterpretation leads to false conclusions in the final report.

docs.title: search_vector_memory → BM25 Score
docs.text:
Range Meaning 0 – 1 Weak match — few overlapping terms 1 – 3 Moderate match — relevant content 3 – 5+ Strong match — highly relevant

BM25 scores are not percentages. They depend on corpus size, document length, and term frequency saturation (k1=1.5, b=0.75). A score of 4.2 means "very relevant", not "42%".

docs.title: correlate_stylometry → Cosine Similarity
docs.text:
Range Interpretation > 0.70 Very likely the same author 0.40 – 0.70 Moderate signal — needs corroboration < 0.15 Unrelated writing styles

Based on character 4-gram frequency vectors with accent folding (Calderón → Calderon). Minimum 40 characters required — shorter samples are silently skipped to avoid false certainty.

docs.title: compare_avatars → Perceptual Hash
docs.text:
Metric Interpretation hamming_distance = 0 Identical images hamming_distance ≤ 10 Probably the same photo (resized, recompressed) hamming_distance > 20 Different images similarity_percentage 0–100% based on hamming distance

Uses difference hash (dHash) which is robust to JPEG compression, resizing, and minor color adjustments.

docs.title: Vector Memory Architecture
docs.text:
During an investigation, every discovered profile with text content (bios, descriptions, titles) is indexed into an in-memory vector store. This allows the agent to cross-reference evidence later.

Profile discovered → tokenize (accent fold + trilingual stem) → TF-IDF vector
                                                               → character 4-gram stylometric vector
                     → index in BM25 store

The vector store is pure Python (no numpy/scipy dependency):

  • Accent folding: unicodedata.normalize("NFD") strips diacritics so calderón matches calderon
  • Trilingual stemming: Light suffix stripping for Spanish, English, and Portuguese (desarrollo → desarr, developer → develop)
  • Stopword removal: 150+ stopwords across ES/EN/PT
  • BM25 scoring: Length-normalized term frequency with IDF weighting (not cosine similarity, which penalized long documents)

docs.title: System Prompt Strategy
docs.text:
The agent's system prompt exists in English and Spanish, and other languages use the English version. It includes:

  1. Role definition — "expert OSINT investigator and Criminal Profiler"
  2. Method — 5-step investigation methodology (start → gather → analyze → pivot → report)
  3. Rules — step limits, no data fabrication, treating tool results as untrusted data
  4. Score interpretation — explicit instructions for BM25, stylometry, and avatar metrics
  5. Report structure — must cover the 6 dimensions
  6. Language — response language matches the investigation

In Spanish, the agent receives instructions in Spanish and responds in "español neutro".

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: osint-d2 agent johndoe --ai-provider deepseek --max-steps 10

docs.title: Web Dashboard
docs.text: Select AI Agent mode in the sidebar configuration, set the AI provider and max steps, then click Start Investigation.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
OSINT_D2_AGENT_MAX_STEPS=10       # Default max reasoning steps
OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek     # Sets the default endpoint and model
OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-...        # Not needed for Ollama
Provider Base URL Model DeepSeek https://api.deepseek.com deepseek-chat OpenAI https://api.openai.com/v1 gpt-4o-mini Ollama http://localhost:11434/v1 llama3 Groq https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 openai/gpt-oss-120b

docs.title: 6D Cognitive Profile
docs.text:
When the agent finishes, it generates a structured analysis. OCEAN Psychology, Ideology & Values, and OpSec / Attack Surface are off by default. Enable them with --sensitive-inferences, the dashboard's Sensitive inferences option, or OSINT_D2_SENSITIVE_INFERENCES=true.

Dimension What the agent analyzes Identity & Demographics Real name, aliases, handle patterns, estimated age, gender, education level. Cross-references names across platforms to identify impersonators. Geo-temporal Timezone inference, location signals, language patterns, activity hours, sleep routine estimation OCEAN Psychology Big Five personality traits inferred from writing style, content choices, and online behavior patterns Tech Stack Programming languages, frameworks, tools, platforms, contribution patterns, skill level indicators Ideology & Values Interests, causes, community affiliations, political signals, content themes OpSec / Attack Surface Password reuse signals, email exposure, handle consistency, data breach exposure, privacy hygiene

Treat the profile as unverified

The personality, ideology, and demographic sections are the model's inferences, not established facts. They can be wrong, and they touch categories that privacy law may specially protect. See Responsible Use.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• More steps = deeper investigation — 6 for quick scans, 10-15 for thorough investigations
  • Trust anchors filter false positives — --trust github:johndoe tells the agent that GitHub profile is confirmed
  • Ollama keeps inference on your machine, but the scans still contact the target sites
  • Check the evidence — the prompt forbids inventing data, but models can still make mistakes
  • Parallel tool calls: some LLMs (GPT-4o) call multiple tools per step, making investigations faster

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: All commands use the osint-d2 entry point. Use osint-d2 <command> --help for full details.

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text:
These options are available across most commands. Run osint-d2 --version for the version.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 failure, 2 invalid usage, 130 interrupted. Results go to stdout, and messages to stderr. Set OSINT_D2_DEBUG=1 to see tracebacks.

Flag Short Description --language -l Output language: en, es, pt, ar, ru --export-json Export results as JSON to reports/ --export-pdf Export a classified-style PDF dossier to reports/ --ai-provider AI provider preset: deepseek, openai, groq, groq-70b, groq-fast, openrouter, huggingface, ollama --ai-key AI API key for that provider (prefer osint-d2 doctor setup-ai, because arguments end up in shell history) --ai-save / --no-ai-save Save the provider and key to the user config. Off by default --proxy Override proxy mode: residential, datacenter --no-proxy Disable proxy for this run even if configured in .env --proxy-country 2-letter country code for geo-targeted proxy (e.g. us) --format table or json. Defaults to table in a terminal, and json when piped --json-raw / --no-json-raw With JSON output, include the raw AI payload --trust Trust anchor (repeatable). Format: network:username or email:address

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doble-2/osint-d2/main/scripts/install-docker.sh
sh install-docker.sh

This creates an osint-d2 folder with the Compose file, a .env for your AI key, and a reports folder.

Open http://localhost:8000 to access the web dashboard.

Batteries Included

The Docker image includes all native dependencies for full functionality:

  • PDF generation — WeasyPrint with Pango, plus Chromium
  • Graph images — Playwright + Chromium pre-installed
  • Web dashboard — all assets vendorized (no external CDN calls)
  • Non-root execution — runs as unprivileged osint user

No additional setup steps required beyond configuring your AI provider.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All OSINT-D2 configuration uses the OSINT_D2_ prefix. Edit your .env file:

docs.title: AI Provider (required — pick one)
docs.text: Variable Description Example OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER Provider name deepseek, openai, ollama OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY API key (not needed for Ollama) sk-xxxxxxxx OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL Provider endpoint (optional) http://ollama:11434/v1 OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL Model to use (optional) deepseek-chat

docs.title: Optional Services
docs.text:
Variable Description OSINT_D2_PROXY_API_KEY ScrapingAnt proxy key for anti-bot bypass OSINT_D2_PROXY_USERNAME ScrapingAnt proxy username OSINT_D2_PROXY_MODE residential or datacenter OSINT_D2_PROXY_COUNTRY 2-letter country code (e.g. us)

Wrong variable names

Previous versions of the documentation used DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY — those are wrong. All variables use the OSINT_D2_ prefix.

docs.title: Passing Variables
docs.text:
.env file (recommended)InlineDocker Compose override 
OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek
OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

docker compose up -d

docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \
  -e OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek \
  -e OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-xxx \
  ghcr.io/doble-2/osint-d2

# docker-compose.override.yml
services:
  osint-d2:
    environment:
      - OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek
      - OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY=sk-xxx

docs.title: LAN / Network Access
docs.text:
By default, Compose publishes the dashboard on 127.0.0.1 only. The dashboard has no authentication: anyone who can reach the port can start investigations (spending your AI credits) and download dossiers. To expose it on a trusted network, set OSINT_BIND. Read Security & Responsible Use first. The server only answers to localhost and 127.0.0.1, to block DNS rebinding, so also list every other address you use in OSINT_D2_CORS_ORIGINS:

OSINT_BIND=0.0.0.0
OSINT_D2_CORS_ORIGINS=http://192.168.1.100:8000,http://my-server.local:8000

docs.title: Ollama (Fully Offline)
docs.text:
Run LLM inference locally, so scan results don't go to an AI provider. Scans still contact the sites being checked.

# docker-compose.override.yml
services:
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"
    volumes:
      - ollama_data:/root/.ollama

  osint-d2:
    environment:
      - OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER=ollama
      - OSINT_D2_AI_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434/v1
      - OSINT_D2_AI_MODEL=llama3.1
    depends_on:
      - ollama

volumes:
  ollama_data:

After starting, pull the model:

docker compose exec ollama ollama pull llama3.1

GPU passthrough

For Nvidia GPUs, add deploy.resources.reservations.devices to the Ollama service. See the Ollama Docker docs.

docs.title: Volumes
docs.text:
Reports are stored in /app/reports inside the container. Mount a local directory to persist them:

volumes:
  - ./reports:/app/reports

Volume permissions

The container runs as user osint (UID 1000). Ensure the mounted directory is writable by UID 1000:

mkdir -p ./reports && chmod 777 ./reports
# or, for tighter permissions:
chown 1000:1000 ./reports

docs.title: Pre-built Image
docs.text:
Pull the latest image from GitHub Container Registry:

docker pull ghcr.io/doble-2/osint-d2:latest
docker run --name osint-d2 -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 --env-file .env ghcr.io/doble-2/osint-d2

The image is built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 by GitHub Actions. It is for running on your own machine: the project does not operate a hosted version.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
The container runs as a non-root user (osint) by default. This provides defense-in-depth: even if Chromium has a sandbox escape vulnerability, the attacker lands in an unprivileged context.

The dashboard page loads all its JavaScript, CSS, and fonts from the image. Investigations still contact the scanned sites and, unless you use Ollama, your AI provider.

The dashboard has no authentication. See Security & Responsible Use.

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
The container includes a built-in health check:

docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}' osint-d2

docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

docs.title: How It Works Under the Hood
AI System Prompts
docs.text:
The agent's prompts live in src/core/services/agent_prompts.py, with one entry per language. A test checks that every language keeps the same rules and score guidance.

EnglishSpanish 
You are an expert OSINT investigator and Criminal Profiler.
Your objective is to build a comprehensive profile of the
target person.

METHOD:
1. Start with what you know (provided username/email)
2. Use the tools to gather evidence from multiple sources
3. Analyze results and decide what to investigate next
4. PIVOT: if you find new emails, usernames, aliases...

RESPONSE LANGUAGE: English.

Eres un investigador OSINT experto y Perfilador Criminalista.
Tu objetivo es construir un perfil completo de la persona
indicada.

MÉTODO:
1. Empieza con lo que sabes (username/email proporcionado)
2. Usa las herramientas para recopilar evidencia
3. Analiza los resultados y decide qué investigar después
4. PIVOTEA: si encuentras emails, usernames, aliases...

IDIOMA DE RESPUESTA: Español neutro.

The prompts also include language-specific score interpretation so the LLM doesn't misinterpret BM25 or stylometric scores.

docs.title: Dashboard Translations
docs.text:
UI translations are stored as JSON files in src/adapters/templates/i18n/:

src/adapters/templates/i18n/
├── en.json    # English (reference)
├── es.json    # Spanish
├── pt.json    # Portuguese
├── ar.json    # Arabic
└── ru.json    # Russian

The FastAPI server loads the appropriate JSON based on ?lang= and injects it into the Jinja2 template. JavaScript runtime strings use a T object:

// In the browser — T is injected by the server
document.getElementById("title").textContent = T.investigation_title;
document.getElementById("start").textContent = T.btn_start;

docs.title: PDF Reports
docs.text: PDF dossiers inherit the language from the investigation. Section headers (IDENTITY & DEMOGRAPHICS, PERFIL PSICOLÓGICO, etc.), labels, and classification tags are all rendered in the selected language.

docs.title: Contributing Translations
docs.text:
To add a new language:

  1. Copy src/adapters/templates/i18n/en.json to <code>.json
  2. Translate all values — keys must remain identical
  3. Add the language to the Language enum in src/core/domain/language.py
  4. Add the system prompts in src/adapters/ai_analyst.py and src/core/services/agent_prompts.py
  5. Add the option to both language selectors in dashboard.html
  6. Add the code to test_i18n_files_share_the_same_keys, then run the tests:
poetry run pytest tests/test_web_server.py

The tests check that every language has the same keys and that the dashboard uses only keys that exist. Keep placeholders such as {target} unchanged in log_* and graph strings.

Tip

The Spanish system prompt uses "español neutro" (neutral Spanish) — avoiding regional slang to maximize clarity for all Spanish-speaking users.

docs.title: Security & Responsible Use
docs.text: OSINT-D2 collects and infers information about people. Treat its server and its output as sensitive.

docs.title: A local tool, not a service
docs.text:
OSINT-D2 is open-source software that you run yourself. For ethical and legal reasons, the project doesn't operate a hosted version, and it never receives your investigations. You decide how to use it, and you are responsible for that use.

The dashboard has no authentication, by design, because it's meant for your own machine. Anyone who can reach it can start investigations, spend your AI credits, and download results if they have the investigation ID. Don't expose it to other people or to the internet.

Setup Default bind osint-d2 serve 127.0.0.1 docker compose up 127.0.0.1 (change with OSINT_BIND) docker run -p 8000:8000 All interfaces. Use -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000

To reach your own instance on a remote machine, use an SSH tunnel:

ssh -L 8000:127.0.0.1:8000 user@server

docs.title: Protecting results
docs.text:
• reports/ holds personal data, so restrict access to it. Set OSINT_D2_REPORT_RETENTION_DAYS to delete old reports automatically, or use osint-d2 purge. Without a retention period, reports stay until you delete them.
  • Unless you use Ollama, scan results are sent to your AI provider. Check that provider's data policy. CLI scans send nothing to an AI provider unless you pass --ai or --deep-analyze.
  • Breach checks send the full email address to Have I Been Pwned.
  • The dashboard keeps the form in the browser tab until you close it. Close the tab on shared machines.
  • API keys saved with osint-d2 doctor setup-ai are stored in a file only your user can read.

docs.title: Untrusted content
docs.text:
Profiles and web pages are written by third parties, and may try to manipulate the agent. OSINT-D2 applies these protections:

Risk Protection Text that gives the LLM instructions Tool results are wrapped as untrusted data and limited in size. This reduces the risk but cannot eliminate it, so review the findings Requests to internal services (SSRF) Agent URLs are checked at every redirect, and private, reserved, and metadata addresses are blocked HTML or scripts in a dossier Report Markdown escapes raw HTML and removes unsafe links PDF rendering Image requests cannot reach internal addresses or follow redirects, and only the dossier itself can be read from disk. The dashboard renders without JavaScript Other sites reaching your local server Unknown hosts are rejected, which blocks DNS rebinding, and so are WebSocket connections from foreign origins

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• DNS rebinding: a hostname that changes its answer between the check and the request can bypass the SSRF check.
  • External requests in PDFs: rendering a dossier fetches its fonts from Google Fonts and the avatars of the profiles found, which reveals your IP address to those servers.

docs.title: Responsible use
docs.text:
Use OSINT-D2 only where you have a lawful basis and, where required, authorization. You are responsible for complying with the laws that apply to you.

Before running or sharing an investigation, keep in mind:

  • Privacy law may apply even to public data. Under the EU's GDPR, for example, collecting and profiling personal data needs a legal basis.
  • Political views and personality are sensitive inferences. They touch categories that can receive extra protection, so personality, ideology, and attack-surface sections are off by default. Get legal advice before enabling them or using them in decisions about someone.
  • Results can be wrong. Namesakes and model errors are common, and the personality and ideology sections are speculative. Do not treat them as fact without corroboration.
  • Do not use it to harass, stalk, or expose anyone.

See also the threat model, acceptable use policy, data flows, and impact assessment template.

To report a vulnerability, see the security policy.

docs.title: Web Dashboard
docs.text:
The dashboard is a local web interface for agent investigations. It streams each step over a WebSocket and lets you download the results when the run finishes.

osint-d2 serve              # http://127.0.0.1:8000
# or
docker compose up -d        # http://localhost:8000

Local tool

The dashboard is meant to run on your own machine, and has no authentication by design. Both commands above listen on loopback only. See Security & Responsible Use.

Finished investigation with the report open (demo data)

docs.title: Run an investigation
docs.text:
1. Enter the subject name. It is required, and it is treated as a person's name, never scanned as a username.
  2. Add what you already know: usernames, emails, and phone numbers, separated by commas.
  3. Optionally add verified accounts (trust anchors) such as github:johndoe or email:john@example.com. They give the agent a verified starting point. Without them, attributions are marked as unconfirmed.
  4. Open Options to change the mode, AI provider, report language, step limit, or breach check.
  5. Click Start Investigation, or press Enter in any field.

The top bar shows the status. Above the results, a bar shows the subject, the current step (such as Step 2 / 6), and the progress. The Console tab opens while the agent works, and Cancel stops the run immediately. When the run finishes, the Report tab opens, or the Graph tab if there is no report.

You can reload the page or change the language at any time: the form stays filled in, and a run in progress reconnects. The status Completed with errors means a tool failed or a file could not be created, so check the console.

On small screens the form collapses when a run starts. Use the arrow next to New investigation to reopen it.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Values Default Mode AI Agent, Telecom AI Agent AI provider DeepSeek, OpenAI, Ollama OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER Language en, es, pt, ar, ru Interface language Max steps 3–15 6 Breach check On, Off (requires OSINT_D2_HIBP_API_KEY) Off

Telecom mode only looks up the phone numbers you enter. It does not use the AI agent and produces no files.

API keys belong to one provider

The dashboard sends OSINT_D2_AI_API_KEY only to the provider set in OSINT_D2_AI_PROVIDER. Selecting a different provider runs without that key, so hosted providers fail with a configuration error until you change .env. Ollama needs no key.

docs.title: Graph
docs.text:
Nodes appear as the agent works. When the run finishes, they are replaced by the final graph: each vertical band is an investigation vector, and the last band holds the conclusions.

To explore it, drag or use the arrow keys to move, and use the wheel, a pinch, the buttons, or + and - to zoom. 0 fits the whole graph.

Handles that look like common first names are labeled as probable false positives.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text:
Each tool call the agent made, in order (demo data)

The timeline appears when the run finishes.

docs.title: Console
docs.text: The console logs each step as it happens, along with warnings and errors.

docs.title: Report
docs.text:
The Report tab shows the main findings and the full analysis. It opens automatically when the agent finishes.

The confidence score is colored by level, but it's the model's own estimate, not a measured probability. Check the evidence before relying on a finding.

docs.text:
Button File PDF Dossier with the graph page Canvas Graph for Obsidian Canvas

The buttons are above the results, next to the subject's name. A button appears only once its file exists. Copies, plus the HTML, SVG, and PNG versions, are saved to reports/.

Change the interface with the selector in the top bar or with ?lang=:

http://localhost:8000/?lang=ar

Arabic uses a right-to-left layout. See Languages for what each language covers.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser
    participant S as FastAPI server
    participant A as Agent engine
    participant T as OSINT tools

    B->>S: POST /api/investigate
    S-->>B: investigation_id
    B->>S: Connect WebSocket
    S-->>B: Replay earlier events
    loop Each step
        A->>T: Call tool
        T-->>A: Result
        A-->>S: Step
        S-->>B: progress, log, node_add
    end
    S-->>B: report_done, graph_svg, timeline
    S-->>B: artifact, status

The dashboard loads all its scripts, styles, and fonts from the local server, so the page itself needs no CDN. Investigations still contact the scanned sites and, unless you use Ollama, your AI provider.

For integrations, see the REST API and the WebSocket protocol.

docs.title: Acceptable Use Policy
docs.text:
Draft

This is a draft for legal review, not legal advice. It has not been reviewed by a lawyer.

OSINT-D2 collects and infers information about people. You run it yourself, and you are responsible for how you use it.

docs.title: Allowed
docs.text:
Use OSINT-D2 only with a lawful basis and, where required, authorization. Examples:

  • Checking your own digital footprint.
  • Authorized security assessments.
  • Journalism and research that follow the laws and ethical rules that apply to you.
  • Investigating fraud or threats, within your legal authority.

docs.title: Not allowed
docs.text:
• Stalking, harassing, threatening, or exposing anyone.
  • Making decisions about employment, housing, credit, insurance, or access to services based on its output.
  • Inferring or recording someone's health, sexuality, religion, politics, or ethnicity without a specific legal basis.
  • Targeting children.
  • Preparing fraud, social engineering, or unauthorized access.
  • Selling or publishing dossiers about people.
  • Breaking the law or the terms of the services you query.

docs.title: Sensitive inferences
docs.text: Personality, ideology, and attack-surface sections are off by default. Enable them only if you have a specific and lawful reason. They are speculative, so don't present them as fact.

docs.title: Your responsibilities
docs.text:
• Confirm findings before relying on them. Namesakes and model errors are common.

docs.title: Deleting data
docs.text:
osint-d2 purge --target johndoe --dry-run   # List the files
osint-d2 purge --target johndoe             # Delete them
osint-d2 purge --older-than 30              # Delete by age

--target needs the exact target. A hunt with several identifiers saves its files under a combined name, so use --dry-run with that name, or --older-than. Copies held by third parties, such as your AI provider, must be requested from them.
